strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: clearly articulates the temporal gap between error introduction and observable conflict in incremental graph construction
Comprehensive three-stage framework: coherent pipeline for conflict detection, error localization, and repair with sensible separation of concerns
Solid technical approach: LCA-based divergence tracing and edge impact scoring with interpretable factors (reachability, conflict count, usage)
Thorough ablation studies: detailed component analysis across multiple models (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, Claude-Haiku) in Tables 1-2
Dataset refinement contribution: systematic 5-step pipeline to remove 160 conflicting edges, providing cleaner testbed with conflict distribution analysis
Version control as engineering contribution: novel application of versioned history capture for graph repair with rollback and tracing capabilities
Good related work grounding: appropriate connections to SLAM, knowledge graphs, and scene graphs
weaknesses: Extremely narrow evaluation scope: limited to 53 interactive fiction environments from single MANGO dataset with no evaluation on other spatial domains or graph reasoning tasks; generalizability highly questionable
Modest absolute performance: best accuracy only 54.88% with concerning failure patterns (Edge-Impact Ranking achieves 75% repair rate but only 45% correctness)
Critical evaluation clarity issues: ground truth determination unexplained, reference graphs not discussed, no validation strategy provided for the 160 edge removals from dataset refinement

Heuristic edge impact scoring lacks principled justification: equal weighting after normalization (Eq. 2) appears ad-hoc; PageRank motivation is hand-wavy without rigorous support; no learned weights or sensitivity analysis

Silent error problem fundamentally unresolved: paper acknowledges persistent undetected errors but provides no statistics on false negative rates or method to address them; severely limits practical utility

Weak baseline comparison: Baseline(GPT-4o) achieves only 5.77% accuracy suggesting poorly designed baseline; no comparison to alternative graph repair, optimization, or constraint satisfaction methods

Limited experimental scope: no ablation on individual impact factors, no sensitivity analysis on 10-iteration repair limit, no evaluation on raw (unrefined) MANGO dataset, no statistical significance testing
Reproducibility concerns: code availability not mentioned, exact prompts to GPT-4o not provided, random seed handling not discussed, computational cost of repair not analyzed
Framework generalization unclear: version control and conflict types are task-specific; unclear how approach would adapt to 3D environments, knowledge graphs, or other spatial reasoning domains
Marginal improvement from combining components: Version Control alone achieves 54.00%, combined method 54.88%—only 0.88 percentage point gain despite added complexity

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: delayed conflicts and error propagation during incremental graph construction are genuine challenges for long-horizon LLM reasoning
Comprehensive three-stage framework thoughtfully integrating conflict detection, error localization via LCA, and version-aware repair
Useful dataset refinement contribution: systematic cleaning of MANGO by removing 160 problematic edges and non-topological actions
Detailed ablation study (Table 1) clearly demonstrating individual component contributions
Clear presentation of problem challenges (Figure 3b) and framework workflow (Figure 2)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (conflict detection, version control, PageRank-inspired scoring, LCA-based error localization) are applications of existing techniques without substantial algorithmic innovation
Concerningly low experimental results: 54.88% accuracy (90/164 repairs) is barely above chance and remains unvalidated for downstream tasks; paper never establishes if this is acceptable

Fundamental limitation inadequately addressed: framework explicitly cannot detect or repair silent errors (acknowledged in text and Figure 3b showing incorrect edge E→J causing no conflict), yet no analysis of prevalence or impact on real-world applicability

Weak evaluation methodology: no downstream task evaluation (e.g., actual navigation queries), no validation that repaired graphs enable correct spatial reasoning, only conflict resolution metrics without measuring graph correctness

Dataset refinement creates reproducibility concerns: 9.6% edge removal makes comparison to original MANGO difficult; refinement process appears manual rather than automated; future work using original benchmark cannot directly compare

Severely underspecified LLM methodology: Section 5 claims LLMs are 'tools for text refinement' but entire repair loop depends on LLM decisions; prompting strategy not described; maximum 10 repair attempts arbitrary; different model behaviors (Table 2) unexplained

Theoretical justification lacking rigor: Edge Impact Score formula (Eq. 2) explicitly acknowledged as 'unprincipled' unweighted sum to avoid hyperparameters; PageRank analogy loose and unjustified; no connection proven between CRG (Eq. 3) and scoring (Eq. 4)

Scalability concerns unaddressed: largest test graph ~70 nodes; MANGO evaluation only used first 70 of 1,264 steps; average 8+ repair iterations per conflict; no computational cost analysis or O(n) complexity discussion

Limited experimental scope: only 53 interactive fiction games; many environments have zero conflicts after refinement; generalization to realistic spatial reasoning unclear; no comparison to knowledge graph repair or graph database consistency techniques

Missing critical analysis: no error categorization (which repairs succeed/fail?), no breakdown by conflict type, no analysis of tradeoffs between different models/methods, incomplete discussion of when framework fails

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine LLM limitations in spatial reasoning with clear articulation of delayed conflicts, entangled errors, and silent errors
Principled three-stage methodology (conflict detection, error localization via LCA, version-controlled repair) with clear separation of concerns
Novel contributions including Version Control mechanism for causal error tracing and Edge Impact Score integrating multiple structural factors
Thorough experimental methodology with honest ablation study (Table 1) and cross-model evaluation demonstrating component contributions
Refined MANGO dataset created through systematic 5-step pipeline providing cleaner evaluation benchmark for future work
Strong presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1-4) and concrete examples clearly illustrating core concepts
weaknesses: Severely limited evaluation scope: only 53 interactive fiction games with small graphs (median ~40 nodes/edges); no evaluation on real-world spatial data, embodied navigation, or other domains; generalization unclear

Modest absolute performance: 54.88% repair accuracy means failures ~45% of the time; gap between repair rate (68.91%) and accuracy indicates many repairs are incorrect; weak baseline (5.77%) limits meaningfulness of comparison

Weak theoretical justification for Edge Impact Score: PageRank connection is informal without proof; uniform weighting across three factors unexplained; no sensitivity analysis; feels like engineering intuition rather than principled design

Dataset refinement introduces evaluation bias: removing pre-existing conflicts means testing on artificially clean data rather than realistic errors; 160 edge removals (9.6%) substantially alter dataset
Silent errors acknowledged but unaddressed: method only repairs detected conflicts despite identifying silent errors as key challenge; no proactive discovery mechanism
Insufficient error localization analysis: paper emphasizes repair success but provides minimal analysis of whether *correct* root causes are identified; no dedicated localization accuracy metrics
Version Control scalability unquantified: no memory cost analysis for long exploration sequences (1,264 steps mentioned); time complexity not discussed

Weak baseline comparison: primary baseline and ablations are internal; no comparison to simple alternatives (sequential removal, FIFO rollback) or other symbolic/learning-based conflict resolution methods
LLM failure modes underexplored: no analysis of when/why LLM makes incorrect repairs; limited discussion of failure cases; missing prompt engineering details
Reproducibility concerns: code unavailable; insufficient implementation detail (e.g., reachability computation method); no statistical significance testing despite small sample sizes in some games

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear articulation of temporal gap between error introduction and conflict manifestation
Comprehensive four-tier evaluation spanning controlled synthetic graphs, cross-vendor testing (7 LLMs), real IF maps, and natural text deployment
Methodologically sound algorithmic validation (Appendix B) separating core algorithm contributions from LLM variability using 1,160 synthetic test cases
Novel technical integration of LCA-based error localization over Reasoning History Tree, providing unified framework for multiple conflict types
Thorough ablation studies (Table 1) clearly demonstrating individual component contributions
Useful dataset contribution: cleaned MANGO variant removing non-topological actions and inconsistencies
Clear presentation with effective visualizations communicating problem space
weaknesses: Severe over-generation in headline result: 4× ground-truth node/edge counts on Dream of the Red Chamber undermines practical utility and contradicts goal of coherent spatial memory

Strong model-dependency without principled solution: optimal configurations differ by model (Table 3), 2 of 7 models show regression (Table 2), proposed held-out validation requires costly LLM inference

Incomplete precision/recall characterization: Table 4 reports only recall; inferred precision ~25% from 4× over-generation unacceptable for structured mapping; Table A3 shows repairs lose 31-89 ground-truth edges indicating problematic trade-off
Severely limited end-to-end evaluation: only Chapters 16-17 of single novel with one repair LLM; authors explicitly acknowledge 'broader literary corpus remains future work'

Minimal baseline comparisons: only simple heuristics; missing comparison to knowledge graph repair, schema-guided error correction, or RAG approaches; heuristic_remove achieves 98 conflicts vs. best LLM at 396-625, challenging LLM repair necessity
Continuous spatial reasoning inadequately addressed: discretization increases false positives, acknowledged but unsolved, severely limiting applicability to natural language

Edge Impact Score lacks theoretical grounding: Equation 2 uses unweighted normalization without justification; perfect Spearman correlation (TC6) on 5-edge sanity-check treated as generalization evidence
Hyperparameter sensitivity: 20-iteration choice driven by volatile 5-game sweep (results: −32.4%, −32.4%, +50.9%, −17.6%); no principled justification for 3 attempts per conflict
Silent errors handled unsystematically: E→J example illustrates issue but framework provides no systematic detection beyond context accumulation
Statistical significance not formally assessed despite modest improvements in many cases and high variance
Version Control computational overhead not quantified; scalability to large graphs not demonstrated
Conflict detection limited to observable violations; cannot detect latent semantic inconsistencies; structurally coherent maps could still be semantically incorrect

strengths: Well-motivated problem identifying critical limitation of LLMs in long-horizon spatial reasoning with clear articulation of temporal gap between error introduction and detection
Sound methodological design with intuitive three-stage pipeline (conflict detection, error localization, version control) and clever use of Reasoning History Tree as DAG for LCA computation
Comprehensive evaluation breadth across four settings (synthetic, TextWorld, real IF maps, literary text) with rigorous component ablation and algorithmic validation independent of LLM variability
Useful dataset contribution: cleaned MANGO benchmark systematically removes pre-existing inconsistencies for controlled evaluation
Generally clear presentation with effective use of figures and concrete examples illustrating conflict resolution
weaknesses: Severe over-generation problem undermines practical utility: predicted nodes/edges reach ~4× ground truth (143 vs 35 nodes, 144 vs 34 edges in Table 4), yet dismissed as 'recall-side improvement'—this produces 3 spurious nodes/edges per real one, fundamentally limiting downstream task utility

End-to-end natural-text evaluation critically limited to single novel (Dream of Red Chamber Chapters 16-17) with single repair LLM (GPT-4.1), providing insufficient generalization evidence for a paper focused on LLM agents

Performance highly inconsistent across models: Table 2 shows regressions for two models; Table 3 shows model-dependent configuration preferences; authors recommend per-model tuning on validation set, suggesting lack of robustness

Edge Impact Score (Eq. 2) lacks theoretical grounding: unweighted sum with ad-hoc normalization, equal weights unjustified, perfect Spearman correlation only on 5-edge toy scenario treated as 'sanity check not statistically robust'

Limited algorithmic novelty: Version Control is standard commit history, LCA is off-the-shelf tree algorithm, Edge scoring simplifies PageRank heuristically; core insight (maintain history, detect conflicts, prioritize) is relatively straightforward

Evaluation rigor gaps: statistical significance not formally assessed at small sample sizes (n=20/30), synthetic experiments inject artificial errors unlike real LLM failures, TextWorld baseline at 16.7% floor effect limits improvement headroom

Repair-versus-preservation trade-off unresolved: LLM repairs lose ground-truth structure (−31 to −89 edges per Table 3 appendix), yet paper provides no principled guidance for configuration selection based on downstream task requirements

Limited baselines and comparisons: only baseline LLM and two simple heuristics, no comparison with knowledge-graph repair methods or other LLM error-correction approaches despite motivating work with SLAM

Conflict detection has fundamental limitations: cannot identify latent semantic inconsistencies only observable structural violations; directional conflicts at high density (8+ errors) degrade to baseline performance; discretization for continuous spaces is ad-hoc and increases false positives

Domain specificity and applicability concerns: method tailored to discrete cardinal directions and unit distances, tested only on navigation/spatial reasoning, relevance to core NLP questionable—appears more aligned with AI systems/robotics

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies and articulates LLMs' limitation in maintaining spatial coherence during long-horizon incremental construction

Elegant technical approach: Separation of Reasoning History Tree (temporal DAG) from spatial graph enables principled LCA-based error localization; unified handling of long-range and local conflicts is theoretically well-motivated

Comprehensive experimental validation: Four evaluation settings (synthetic, TextWorld, real IF maps, natural text), cross-vendor sweep across 7 LLMs, algorithmic validation independent of LLM (Appendix B showing 2.3× speedup), clear ablation study demonstrating component contributions
Solid methodology: Three-stage pipeline is principled; LCA formulation correct; Edge Impact Scoring well-motivated by PageRank; 42 real IF maps with 534 conflicts provide substantial testbed
Honest limitations discussion: Authors clearly identify over-generation (4×), model-dependent behavior, degradation at high error density, and limited end-to-end coverage
Clear presentation: Figures 2–3 effectively communicate framework and challenge scenarios; challenge scenario effectively illustrates why detection and localization must be separated
Dataset contribution: Cleaned MANGO variant removing non-topological actions and pre-existing inconsistencies provides controlled testbed for future work
weaknesses: Severe over-generation problem: Predicted nodes/edges reach ~4× ground truth on Dream of the Red Chamber (Table 4), producing ~3× more structure than exists. No analysis of whether this is inherent to discretization or solvable; no mitigation strategies explored; significantly constrains practical applicability

Limited end-to-end natural-text evaluation: Only Chapters 16–17 of one novel evaluated end-to-end with single repair LLM (gpt-4.1). Generalization to other novels/genres/domains completely unclear. Algorithmic mechanisms (Tables 2–3) validated separately but not this pipeline

Model-dependent results requiring validation tuning: Table 3 shows different models prefer different modes (EI for GPT-5.5, VC+EI for Claude-Haiku). Authors recommend running both on validation sets to select, adding deployment complexity with unclear selection criteria

High-density direction-conflict degradation: VC+EI drops to 25% CF rate on 8 simultaneous directional errors (Table 1), representing practical ceiling. Unscaffolded LLMs can match/exceed scaffolded modes in this regime, questioning framework value

Incomplete algorithmic validation: Edge scoring shows perfect correlation (ρ=1.0) only on 5-edge sanity check (Table A2), explicitly treated as non-robust. Large-scale validation (1,160 graphs) shows 81.12% error retention and only 42.4% for naming conflicts

Discretization strategy underspecified: 'Angles binned into directional categories' and 'elastic optimization based on conflict severity' lack concrete algorithmic detail. Reproducibility concern for real-text deployment
Limited baseline comparisons: Only unscaffolded LLM and two simple heuristics; no comparison to alternative graph repair, SLAM-inspired methods, or other consistency-maintenance strategies

Repair-vs-preservation tradeoff: LLM modes cannot match heuristic_remove's absolute residual reduction (98 vs. 396–625), suggesting fundamental limitation. Unclear whether this is inevitable or improvable
Silent error analysis lacking: Acknowledged but not empirically quantified. No characterization of how many silent errors remain or systematic patterns
Version Control overhead unanalyzed: Memory costs, complexity of diff/rollback operations, and scalability to long explorations not addressed
No statistical significance testing: Acknowledged for n=20/30 experiments; some confidence intervals in Table 1 quite wide (30–70%). System prompts not provided, limiting reproducibility
